slide-006.title: Macro-Environmental Analysis - Environmental Factors Analysis
body: Analysis of trends and causes:
The resulting inspiration or impact on the company:

Phenomenal/Trend 1: COREPLAND, CALIFORNIA
Focus on reducing carbon emissions from non-road equipment. Through carbon credits and financial incentives, the Planned encourages the purchase of low- or zero-emission engineering machinery. Equipment involved in Planned can obtain carbon credits that can be used to reduce operating costs or trade in the carbon market and further increase returns on investment. The objective of COREplanned is to phase out high-emission equipment and promote a green transformation of the industry.
Scenario/trend 2: Market penetration of new energy products is slower
While California is at the forefront in promoting electric engineering machinery and provides incentives such as COREplanned, in other states government support is relatively weak and market incentives are limited. This difference has led to varying rates of diffusion of electric engineering machinery throughout the country and significant differences in market acceptance. Many states continue to rely on traditional energy equipment, limiting market penetration of electric engineering machinery.
Phenomenals/trend 3: Hazard materials

phenomena/trend 4: Environmental and climate adaptation aspects
The United States is a vast country with diverse climatic and geographic conditions, covering extremes such as extreme cold and high heat. This requires engineering machinery to be more adaptable and able to operate steadily in different environments. In addition, users have different needs for equipment selections, such as freezing in extreme cold areas and increased heat radiation in high-heating areas.

1. To accelerate the process of certification of electrical products, to facilitate their import, to actively participate in planned, to promote standard electric and hybrid equipment, to assist customers in obtaining carbon credits, and to enhance market awareness of environmental equipment.

2. New energy products are difficult to generate revenue in the United States in the short term. However, from the point of view of technology reserves, an attempt could be made to introduce electrical products for adaptive certification in California.

3. Strict compliance with U.S. hazardous materials regulations to ensure that exported equipment meets RCRA and CERCLA requirements. At the same time, supply chain management has been strengthened to ensure compliance in material procurement.
4. Each product line requires a package of extreme weather events such as high heat and cold. This meets market requirements while increasing the profitability of products.

slide-007.title: Macro-environmental analysis - Political - Analysis of political factors
body: Analysis of trends and causes:
The resulting inspiration or impact on the company:

Case/trend 1: Significant tariff escalation
Trump currently imposes a tariff of 55 per cent on Chinese products. China ' s exports of construction equipment products to the United States market are directly affected, and there will be no fundamental turnaround in the short run of the trade war.
Symptoms/trend 2: The rise of trade protectionism
The first is the risk of anti-dumping investigations, and the United States has now launched a new round of “double back” investigations into XCMG high machine products. Instead of technical and certification barriers, TRP governments may increase market access difficulties for XCMG products by raising the threshold for technology certification (e.g. environmental requirements, safety standards). In addition, the United States Government may require more infrastructure projects to use local brands or “United States-made” products and further reduce market space for Chinese brands.
Scenario/trend 3: Increased geopolitical risk
The United States may impose stricter controls on Chinese construction equipment products, such as enhanced spot checks at the import chain, increased frequency of inspections or fine-tuning of inspection standards (e.g. mechanical performance, material composition, environmental indicators, etc.), further making exports more difficult.

Increased tariffs can directly affect the profitability of XCMG products and require pre-positioning of high tariffs for products such as equipment and friendly bank guarantee schemes.
2. In order to deal with possible reductions in the space available for the survival of Chinese products as a result of trade protection, the competitiveness of products should be enhanced from product controllability, operational efficiency, control and equity to ensure their value for money relative to competitive advantages.

3. Great importance needs to be attached to the completeness and accuracy of the product TCF documents, which will be reviewed and optimized expeditiously by the Joint General Research Institute and the Plant Research Institute under the leadership of USRO.

Standard flatbed trailer

Standard flatbed trailers are a very common type of trailer. While they have several different dimensions (including 24, 40, 45, 48 and 53 feet), 48-foot flatbed trailers are the most commonly used. Multifunctionality is a key feature of these trailers. Usually used for the transport of steel, construction equipment, wood and other open commodities, flat-board vehicles are open on their backs and sides to facilitate handling through forklifts or scooters. The maximum height and width of any cargo transported using these trailers is 8 feet 6 inches (2591 mm), which can be used for the bulk transport of 8 tons of microcompact excavator products. The flat-bed trailer is five feet from the ground, with a maximum load of 48,000 pounds (2177kg). Because it does not have a container to accommodate its contents (such as dry vans), standard flatbed trailers can be used for the transport of super-large cargo, provided the necessary permits are obtained and appropriate routes are followed. Standard flat-bed trailers and all other trailers must be fixed correctly with chain, tape and various tarpaulin solutions.

Transport scenes - the usual type of transport engine
Landing/staircase trailer

When the height of the cargo is a constraint, landing or staircase trailers are often used as alternatives to flat-bed trailers. The simplicity of flat-board vehicles, combined with their increased high capacity, makes land-fall trailers a common mode of transport. The surface trailers, consisting of top decks and rear parts close to the ground level, can drag cargo up to a height of 10 feet and 2 inches (3099 mm) to be considered as exceeding the standard. The flat-board vehicle is usually five feet from the ground, while the landing trailer is much shorter at a minimum of three foot six inches. In the 53-foot pattern, these trailers have 10 and 43-foot lengths on deck and below deck, respectively. Because of its multifunctional nature and ability to carry higher cargoes, staircase trailers are a widely available option among global carriers. You usually see tow trailers carrying agricultural and construction materials, as well as various types of machinery that are suitable for a 10-foot 2-inch limit.
